newsitem.title: UK: UK govt invites bids for traffic control PFI deals.
newsitem.headline: UK govt invites bids for traffic control PFI deals.

text.p: The UK government has invited private sector companies to submit bids to build and operate five Regional Traffic Control Centres across the English road network - a move to help cut traffic jams, it said on Monday.

The new project was announced by the Highways Agency, an offshoot of the UK Department of Transport. Transport minister John Watts said it had set up a consultation process to establish the traffic centres.
The centres will assist the police in managing traffic and warn motorists in advance of delays on motorways and main roads.
They will also collect traffic data and help handle roadside emergencies.

Watts said in a press statement: "Traffic volumes are continuing to grow and by the year 2025 pressure on the network could almost double. It is therefore very important that we find more innovative ways of getting the best use out of our existing roads.
The Department of Transport said it was unable to quantify how much the private finance contracts were worth.
